_comment: Pin table for third-party wheels handed to PipliteAddon.piplite_urls, so the
kernel resolves them from this site's own origin instead of PyPI at boot.
WHY ANY OF THIS EXISTS: ipykernel depends on `comm`, which ships in neither
pyodide-lock.json (359 packages) nor the pyodide-kernel extension's own piplite
index (ipykernel, piplite, pyodide-kernel, widgetsnbextension). Before it was
vendored, every single boot fetched it from pypi.org + files.pythonhosted.org.
scripts/repl_smoke.py's --offline gate is what surfaced that.
WHY A PIN FILE AND NOT A COMMITTED WHEEL: R6/R8 (check_wheel_coherence.py
--check-untracked) require ZERO tracked .whl files repo-wide, with no allowlist.
The ADR's reasoning is provenance -- it retired the hand-committed pylibftdi
binary with 'the hand-committed binary with no recipe is retired, not relocated'.
A committed comm wheel was the same shape: a binary in git whose only recipe was
a prose README. scripts/fetch_piplite_wheels.py is that recipe. Wheels land in
web-repl/vendor/piplite-wheels/, which .gitignore already covers via /vendor/.
TO ADD ONE: append an entry here, add the matching path to piplite_urls in
jupyter_lite_config.json, add the package name to required[] if the kernel cannot
boot without it, then rebuild and re-run the offline gate -- it is the only check
that proves the wheel is used rather than silently fetched from PyPI.
TO UPDATE A VERSION: change version + sha256 together. The fetcher verifies the
download against BOTH this sha and PyPI's own published digest, and refuses on
any mismatch rather than publishing an unverified file.

wheels.name: comm
wheels.why: ipykernel dependency; in neither pyodide-lock.json nor the piplite index
